tasks.short: Attend the yearly first-aid refresher, practise scenarios, keep the certificate on file and read guideline updates.

steps.what: Shuttle driver attends the yearly first-aid refresher course
Shuttle driver practises first-aid procedures with colleagues
Shuttle driver hands a copy of the certificate to the office
Shuttle driver reads updates to first-aid guidelines

tasks.design: The training provider reports completed courses directly to the employer's learning system ({LMS}), which keeps the certificate and books the next refresher before it expires. Courses, practice and reading stay with the driver.
tasks.previous_blocker: Certificates were copied by hand and expiry tracked on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems take course results from providers and send reminders.
tasks.still_hard: First aid is a hands-on skill that fades without practice.
tasks.human_edge: Staying calm and acting when a passenger collapses.

reach.learn: Whether automatic booking keeps certificates current.

evidence.claim: Learning systems take course results from providers and send reminders before expiry.
Employers must have enough trained first-aiders for their work.

assumptions: Boundary: from course booking to current knowledge; giving first aid is outside.
Input contract: course results sent by the training provider; fallback is paper copies.
Courses, practice and reading do not change.
Office time is outside the driver's savings.

incremental.description: Shuttle driver confirms the booked refresher date.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Almost all of this task is training in person.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write mileage and times, write the route and stops, note delays with reasons, and hand in the log.

steps.what: Shuttle driver writes start and end mileage and times in the trip log
Shuttle driver records vehicle routes and stops in the log
Shuttle driver notes deviations and delays with the reason
Shuttle driver hands in the trip log at the office

tasks.design: The vehicle's telematics unit and the driver app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) record trips, mileage, times and stops against the planned run during working hours only. The driver picks a reason for any delay from a list, and the trip report is a dashboard for the dispatcher. Data are not used to score drivers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Trip logs were written by hand and handed in at the end of the shift.
tasks.enabler_now: Telematics and driver apps record trips.
tasks.still_hard: Location data watch drivers; use must be limited and agreed.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining why the airport run took the long way round.

reach.learn: Whether automatic trip records cut disputes with clients.

evidence.claim: Webfleet Tachograph Manager downloads and archives tachograph data remotely and alerts on remaining driving time.
Telematics and driver apps observe location and behaviour, so the works council must consent.
The French regulator fined a logistics firm EUR 32 million for scanner indicators of idle time and long retention.

assumptions: Boundary: from the trip to the trip report; client invoicing is outside.
Input contract: planned runs from the dispatcher; fallback is the paper log.
Noting delay reasons stays with the driver.
unknowns: Whether the works council agrees to telematics.
research_questions: Do client disputes about trips fall?

incremental.description: Shuttle driver checks the day's trip record at shift end.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Firms without telematics keep paper logs.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Talk with passengers about the area, look up places on the phone and hand out leaflets and maps.

steps.what: Shuttle driver provides passengers with information about the local area and points of interest
Shuttle driver looks up restaurants, hotels and opening hours on the phone at stops
Shuttle driver hands out leaflets and maps

tasks.design: The dispatch office keeps a short city guide in the driver app ({OTHER}) with hotels, restaurants and sights near each stop, so the driver finds details quickly; a QR code in the vehicle opens the same guide for passengers instead of paper leaflets. Talking with passengers stays with the driver; no chatbot answers them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drivers searched the web at stops and carried paper leaflets.
tasks.enabler_now: Driver apps can hold a curated guide, and QR codes link passengers to it.
tasks.still_hard: Guides go out of date; opening hours change.
tasks.human_edge: Recommending the right place for this guest, not the first in the list.

reach.learn: Whether a shared guide keeps advice consistent.

evidence.claim: Driver apps can hold a curated city guide, and a QR code can link passengers to it.

assumptions: Boundary: from passenger questions to information given; bookings for passengers are outside.
Input contract: city guide kept by the dispatch office; fallback is web search and leaflets.
Talking with passengers does not change.
Dispatch time keeping the guide is outside the driver's savings.
research_questions: Do passengers use the QR guide?

incremental.description: Shuttle driver reports outdated guide entries.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is conversation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take fares and make change, check vouchers, issue receipts, count cash and fill the cash sheet, and hand cash in.

steps.what: Shuttle driver collects fares from passengers and makes change
Shuttle driver checks vouchers and booking confirmations
Shuttle driver writes receipts by hand
Shuttle driver counts cash and fills in the cash sheet at shift end
Shuttle driver hands cash in at the office

tasks.design: A mobile payment terminal linked to the booking system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) takes cards and phones, so less cash changes hands, and scans booking QR codes and vouchers. Once the driver confirms the fare on the terminal, it prints or e-mails the receipt. Card payments reconcile automatically, so only cash is counted and handed in.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fares were mostly cash, receipts handwritten and cash sheets filled by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Mobile terminals take cards and phones, scan QR codes and issue receipts.
tasks.still_hard: Some passengers only pay cash; the cash flow stays for them.
tasks.human_edge: Sorting out a fare dispute politely at the kerb.

reach.learn: Whether card terminals cut end-of-shift cash work.

evidence.claim: Mobile payment terminals take cards and phones, scan QR codes and print or e-mail receipts.
Payment records must be kept seven years for tax.

assumptions: Boundary: from boarding to cash handed in; client invoicing is outside.
Input contract: bookings and vouchers from the booking system; fallback is cash and paper.
Cash passengers are served as now.
Office time is outside the driver's savings.
unknowns: Share of fares paid in cash.
research_questions: Do cash differences at shift end fall?

incremental.description: Shuttle driver charges and checks the terminal.

approvals.approved_version: The fare as confirmed by the driver on the terminal in s1; a changed fare needs a new confirmation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Routes with many cash passengers save less.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The shuttle driver keeps driving, passengers and first aid; trip logs, receipts and most cash work go.
skills_to_grow: Using the driver app and terminal
role.ambitious_version: A driver who ends the shift without paperwork.
